passages.text: But perhaps one of you has thought that someone can be made into something else by another, but cannot himself transform himself into whatever he wishes, and that changing belongs to one who grows old and has to die .....; but this should not be thought of immortals. For did not angels, ageless ...... and of fiery substance, change into flesh, and those with Abraham who were ..........., whose feet people also washed as though those beings were humans of the same substance? An angel also wrestled with Jacob, who was a human, turning into flesh so that he could come into bodily contact with him. And, having wrestled, he likewise turned back to his own nature when he wished. Having now changed into fire, he did not burn Jacob's broad tendon, but inflamed it and made him lame. One who cannot become something else when he wishes is mortal, being subject to his own nature. But one who can become what he wishes when he wishes, mastering nature itself and returning to youth, is immortal. Therefore, all the more, God's power transforms the body's substance into whatever he wishes whenever he wishes, and brings forth something of the same substance with no transformation present, but not of equal power. For the one who brings it forth can also bring about its turning back toward himself into another substance. But the one brought forth, being also a child of the transformation from that one, cannot become anything else without the will of the one who brought it forth, unless that one wishes.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The infinitive with having is read as the prospect or necessity of dying in the context of aging and mortality. The five-dot gap remains a gap; no lost adverb, noun, or other completion is supplied. A capacity-to-die emphasis is a material alternative to has to die.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οἱ παρὰ τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ........... σθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: and those with Abraham who were ...........
lexical_decisions.rationale: The eleven-dot gap conceals the participle's lexical stem. Only its surviving passive plural ending licenses generic were in the English; no specific action such as appearing, dining, or being received is restored. The Abraham phrase and the following feet-washing clause are both retained.
The supplied ὁμῶς is taken in its alike or likewise sense rather than silently normalized to the adversative accent ὅμως. A contextual nevertheless interpretation remains possible but is not imposed.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ πλατὺ νεῦρον οὐκ ἔκαυσε μέν, ἔφλεξε δέ
lexical_decisions.chosen: he did not burn ... the broad tendon, but inflamed it
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both the broad tendon and the contrast between the two fire verbs are retained. Scorched is a material alternative for the second verb; inflamed makes the distinction intelligible without adding an otherwise unexpressed severing or consuming of the tendon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁμοούσιον μὴ παρούσῃ τροπῇ προβάλλει, ἰσοδύναμον δὲ οὔ
lexical_decisions.chosen: brings forth something of the same substance with no transformation present, but not of equal power
lexical_decisions.rationale: Same substance and equal power are explicitly distinguished. The participial phrase states the absence of a present transformation; its exact relation to the bringing forth is left broad rather than expanded into a specific material mechanism.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὁ μὲν προβάλλων καὶ εἰς ἑτέραν πάλιν οὐσίαν ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν τραπέντα δύναται
lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who brings it forth can also bring about its turning back toward himself into another substance
lexical_decisions.rationale: The ability verb is elliptical, with the surrounding transformation account supplying the action and the accusative participle supplying the thing turned. The main text reads the turn as belonging to the brought-forth thing, with back toward himself referring to its producer. A material alternative understands the producer's own return to another substance through a loose shift of construction; the accusative participle more directly supports the object-oriented main reading. No specific additional power or physical procedure is supplied.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὧν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ὡς ὁμοουσίων ἀνθρώπων ἄνθρωποι ἔνιψαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: whose feet people also washed as though those beings were humans of the same substance
lexical_decisions.rationale: Also explicitly represents the καί within this feet-washing clause, separately from the earlier and those with Abraham representing καὶ οἱ. Even their feet were washed is a viable emphatic reading of this particle; the additive main rendering retains the surviving wording without supplying content within the eleven-dot gap.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints five dots. The English preserves exactly five dots, without recovering or supplying the unavailable content.
The selected edition prints six dots after the ageless expression. The English preserves exactly six dots and translates the surviving fiery-substance description, without restoring the missing link.

The selected edition prints eleven dots followed by the surviving ending σθέντες. The English preserves exactly eleven dots, with only generic passive were representing the surviving inflection. The ending's unavailable lexical stem is not restored, and no complete original wording is claimed.

passages.text: When the advance messenger had reported these things, Peter looked directly at our father and said, “Do you hear, Faustus? Your transformation was brought about by Simon the magician, as is now evident. Thinking that Caesar was seeking him for harm, he fled in fear, placing his own form upon you so that, when you died, grief would come upon your children.” Hearing this, our father wept and lamented, saying, “You have judged correctly, Peter. Annoubion ...... of mine, because he loved me, cryptically disclosed the plot, and I did not believe.........., since I deserved to suffer.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπὸ Σίμωνος τοῦ μάγου ἡ μεταμόρφωσίς σου γέγονεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Your transformation was brought about by Simon the magician
lexical_decisions.rationale: The construction presents Simon as the agent responsible for Faustus’s altered appearance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Καίσαρος γὰρ νομίσας ἐπὶ κακῷ αὐτὸν ζητεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thinking that Caesar was seeking him for harm
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπὶ κακῷ indicates harmful or punitive intent without specifying the precise punishment. The contextual interpretation of Caesar as the seeker is retained despite the printed case irregularity disclosed in source_issues.

lexical_decisions.chosen: placing his own form upon you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The concrete image of putting Simon’s appearance around or upon Faustus is retained rather than reduced to simple resemblance.
μυστηριωδῶς indicates an indirect, mysterious, or cryptic disclosure; ἐπιβουλή is a hostile plot or design.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὐκ ἐπίστευ.........., ἐπειδὴ τοῦ παθεῖν ἤμην ἄξιος
lexical_decisions.chosen: and I did not believe.........., since I deserved to suffer
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first-person speaker and the following first-person ἤμην support “I,” but the precise ending of ἐπίστευ- and any further lost wording remain unavailable. The English does not supply an object of belief.

The main rendering takes φιλέω as affection and the present participle causally: his affection motivates the confidential warning. This is supported by 20.11, where Faustus calls Annoubion and Appion friends from his earliest age, and by Annoubion’s disclosure of the hostile plot here. The materially different while kissing me is also viable: φιλέω can denote kissing, and the participle may describe an accompanying action rather than its cause. The main text does not claim that affection is the only lexical sense or that a concomitant kiss is excluded.

source_issues.source_quote: Καίσαρος γὰρ νομίσας ἐπὶ κακῷ αὐτὸν ζητεῖν
source_issues.issue: The edition prints the genitive Καίσαρος, although the contextual reading takes Caesar as the subject of ζητεῖν, for which the accusative Καίσαρα would ordinarily be expected in this infinitival construction after νομίσας. Καίσαρα is only a proposed grammatical regularization; the translation retains the contextually defensible interpretation without claiming that the regularization is printed.

The selected edition prints a six-dot lacuna before μού. The surviving “of mine” indicates a lost description or relationship, but its wording cannot be recovered. All six dots remain explicit, and no description is restored.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ οὐκ ἐπίστευ.........., ἐπειδὴ τοῦ παθεῖν ἤμην ἄξιος
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints ten dots immediately after the surviving verbal stem ἐπίστευ-. The precise verbal ending and any following words are unavailable; the ten-dot gap is retained without supplying an object or other lost content.
